name: United States (Union)

areaKm2.note: The world_1815 "United States" polygon (5.53M km2 on the sphere) spans the contiguous US incl. the South, so the map overstates the Union and overlaps the Confederacy. Union area 1863 = contiguous US ~8.0M km2 minus the 11 seceded states ~1.95M = ~6.1M km2 incl. western territories.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1863 = 34,026k for the whole United States; 1860 census: free states ~18.9M, loyal slave states (MD, DE, KY, MO) ~2.6M, West Virginia ~0.38M, territories ~0.25M = ~22.1M in 1860, grown to ~23M by 1863. Excludes the 11 seceded states.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) United States 1860 = 19.8% (places of 2,500+); the free states were more urban (~25%) than the South.

activePersonnel.note: Livermore, Numbers and Losses (1900) p. 47: 918,121 on the Union army rolls on 1 January 1863 (present and absent). Union army page: ~700,000 peak present. Mid = present army ~700,000 plus ~34,000 in the navy; high = rolls plus navy.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: state militia callable for emergencies (Pennsylvania and New York militia in June-July 1863) and the first draftees of the March 1863 Enrollment Act.

supportPersonnel.note: Field and heavy artillery ~45,000, engineers, signal corps, quartermaster and medical ~20,000, navy ~34,000 in 1863 (84,415 served over the whole war, Union navy page). Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Union army page: 2,128,948 enlisted over the war (~9.6% of the Union population cumulatively); peak strength ~1.0M on the rolls in May 1865 (Livermore) = 4.4% at one time.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry present, all departments, mid-1863: ~80% of the ~700,000 present (Livermore's returns). Army of the Potomac at Gettysburg ~94,000 present.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Springfield and Enfield rifle-muskets; first Spencer repeaters

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: volunteer regiments, veteran by 1863, new regiments raw

count.note: Union cavalry present, mid-1863 (all US cavalry fought as mounted infantry and light horse; Brandy Station June 1863).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: breech-loading carbines (Sharps, Burnside), Spencers from 1863

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: improving after 1863 reorganisation under Pleasonton

count.note: Educated guess: field guns in ~400 light batteries; the Army of the Potomac had ~370 guns at Gettysburg.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Parrott rifles, 3-inch Ordnance rifles, 12-pdr Napoleons

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Hunt's artillery reserve broke Pickett's Charge

count.note: Seagoing ironclads (Passaic-class monitors, New Ironsides, Roanoke) and screw frigates and sloops, mid-1863. The page: the fleet grew more than fifteen-fold to 671 vessels by 1865.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: turreted monitors with 15-inch Dahlgrens

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: expanded with merchant officers

count.note: Gunboats, converted steamers and river ironclads (Eads gunboats) of the blockading and Mississippi squadrons; the page gives 671 vessels at the end of the war; the mid-1863 count is interpolated.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: converted merchant steamers and purpose-built double-enders

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: blockade duty experience

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5. Evidence: Meade at Gettysburg, Grant at Vicksburg; uneven corps commanders; no general staff

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: state volunteer regiments with local identity

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Gettysburg and Vicksburg in July 1863 after Fredericksburg and Chancellorsville; draft riots

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: rifle-muskets, rifled artillery, early repeaters

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none / cuirass). Evidence: no body armour; armoured trains and river ironclads

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: turret monitors, the first fleet of them

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Washington defences (~68 forts), field entrenchment

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: US Military Railroad, river steamers, 590 ocean-going chartered vessels (Union army page)

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: US Military Telegraph, signal corps flag and torch

isr.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Union Army Balloon Corps (to August 1863), cavalry, Bureau of Military Information

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID) United States 1863 = 4,734 for the whole country; the free states had ~10-15% higher income per head than the national mean (Engerman), so the Union is put at ~5,200.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds): 1860 = 7,060 (~0.8% of GNP, low), 1863 = 119,662 (~$580M). Against a Union GNP of ~$4.5bn that is ~13-15%.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: manufacturing about a fifth to a quarter of northern output in 1860.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: large grain exporter (wheat to Britain during the war).

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population. Young population, the true share was probably at the high end.

artillery.note: Educated guess: field and siege guns per year from West Point Foundry, Fort Pitt, Watervliet and contractors.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: monitors and seagoing warships completed per year 1863-64.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess: gunboats built or converted per year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: turnpikes, plank and macadam roads in the northern states.

railKm.note: CHAT (https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta) railline United States 1863 = 52,388 km; about 14,500 km (9,000 miles) lay in the Confederacy in 1861 (McPherson, isbn:0-19-503863-0, ch. 10), part of it Union-held by 1863.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Portsmouth NH, Hampton Roads, New Orleans, San Francisco, Port Royal, Key West.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 4,225k tons (United States 1863, incl. coastal, lake and river tonnage; flight from the flag reduced it during the war, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: armies tied to railheads and rivers, wagon trains beyond.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: about 70% of the 1860 US stock of ~6.2M horses and 1.1M mules.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 rows: familiar terrain and population support; Washington ringed with forts.

notes: Snapshot = the Union in July 1863 (Gettysburg, Vicksburg). Population = loyal states incl. Maryland, Delaware, Kentucky, Missouri, West Virginia and territories; the seceded states are the confederate-states snapshot; includes is empty. Border caveat: no basemap file separates the Union from the Confederacy; hb:1815:United States covers both and overlaps the confederate-states area. Personnel: army present and navy = active; militia and draftees = trainedReserves. Strengths from Livermore (1900, Internet Archive text) and the Union army and Union navy pages. Branch split and artillery count are reconstructions (grade C/D).
